executive_summary: Today's intelligence picture is defined by two converging pressures: the accelerating militarization of technology and infrastructure, and the institutional strain on the oversight bodies meant to govern both. U.S. strikes on Iranian military sites, the live-fire validation of autonomous combat drones, and Gulf states modeling AI infrastructure defense on Ukraine's wartime experience all signal that the threshold between conventional conflict and technology-enabled warfare is narrowing rapidly, with adversaries and partners alike recalibrating around that reality. Simultaneously, the domestic governance architecture appears under stress — the DNI nominee faces Senate scrutiny over election integrity, the Space Force contends with budget cuts and a leadership vacuum, Congress is pushing back on Pentagon autonomy through the FY2027 NDAA, and CISA is simultaneously launching new vulnerability programs while adding to its actively exploited catalog, suggesting demand is outpacing institutional capacity. The Iranian thread is particularly worth tracking: U.S. kinetic strikes, Gulf concern about Iranian cyberattacks on AI infrastructure, and the Dutch dismantling of a crypto fraud network with potential state-adjacent financing implications all point to Iran as a through-line across military, geopolitical, and financial domains today. sections.title: Cyber
sections.intro: Today's cyber landscape features a new AI-driven vulnerability management initiative from the Trump administration, a major genetic data breach settlement, and fresh additions to CISA's active exploit catalog.

items.headline: Trump Administration Launches AI-Powered 'Gold Eagle' Vulnerability Clearinghouse
items.summary: The administration unveiled Gold Eagle, a program using AI to help government, industry, and critical infrastructure operators detect, prioritize, and patch vulnerabilities faster. The initiative signals a shift toward AI-assisted triage at scale, which could meaningfully reduce the window between disclosure and remediation. Watch whether adoption mandates follow for federal agencies and whether private sector uptake is voluntary or incentivized.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: CISA Adds Two Actively Exploited Vulnerabilities to Known Exploited Catalog
items.summary: CISA flagged two newly confirmed exploited vulnerabilities, including CVE-2023-4346 affecting the KNX building automation protocol — a sector with direct critical infrastructure exposure. Active exploitation of industrial and building control protocols is a persistent concern given the difficulty of patching operational technology environments. Federal agencies face binding remediation deadlines under BOD 22-01.

items.headline: 23andMe Pays $18 Million to Settle Multi-State Data Breach Claims
items.summary: A coalition of 42 state attorneys general secured an $18 million settlement from 23andMe over cybersecurity failures that exposed sensitive genetic and personal data in a breach affecting millions of users. The settlement underscores growing state-level enforcement muscle on data security, particularly for companies holding biometric or health-adjacent data. With 23andMe having filed for bankruptcy, the case also raises questions about what protections consumers retain when breached companies become insolvent.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: CISA and Allies Release Joint Guidance on Building Vulnerability Disclosure Programs
items.summary: CISA, NSA, and international partners published joint best-practice guidance for software manufacturers and service providers on establishing coordinated vulnerability disclosure programs, including CVE assignment and triage processes. The timing alongside the Gold Eagle announcement suggests a coordinated push to systematize how vulnerabilities flow from discovery to remediation across the ecosystem. Organizations without formal CVD programs should treat this as a baseline benchmark.

sections.title: Geopolitical
sections.intro: Active conflict zones from the Black Sea to Sudan are reshaping regional power dynamics, while the Iran war's aftershocks continue to reverberate through Gulf infrastructure, U.S. defense policy, and Middle East diplomacy.

items.headline: Russia Escalates Economic Warfare Against Ukraine by Targeting Black Sea Trade Infrastructure
items.summary: Moscow has shifted military focus toward Ukraine's deepwater ports and Black Sea trade routes in a deliberate campaign to strangle Kyiv's wartime economy. The strategy mirrors historical naval blockade logic — denying revenue and supply chains rather than contesting front lines. Watch whether NATO allies respond with expanded maritime security commitments or accelerated arms transfers to protect port infrastructure.

items.headline: Gulf States Look to Ukraine's Wartime Resilience as Model for Protecting AI Infrastructure from Iranian Attacks
items.summary: Iranian strikes on Gulf infrastructure have raised urgent questions about the viability of ambitious AI investment programs in the region, with Ukraine's experience keeping critical systems operational under sustained bombardment offering a potential playbook. The convergence of kinetic conflict and high-value technology infrastructure marks a new frontier in economic warfare. Gulf states' ability to insulate AI projects from disruption will significantly affect their long-term strategic positioning relative to both Iran and global tech competition.

items.headline: FY2027 NDAA Reflects Congress's Effort to Claw Back Oversight of a Pentagon in Political Turmoil
items.summary: Both House and Senate versions of the FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act contain provisions designed to constrain Pentagon policy discretion, driven by congressional anger over the Iran War and politically motivated dismissals of senior military leaders. The legislation signals a deepening civil-military rift at the institutional level, not merely the rhetorical one. How much of this oversight language survives conference and reconciliation will reveal whether Congress can meaningfully check executive control of defense policy in a wartime environment.

items.headline: Sudan Sanctions Expand as UN Evidence of Atrocities Mounts, but Key Enablers Remain Shielded
items.summary: New sanctions have been imposed on Sudan amid accumulating evidence of war crimes and possible genocide, yet the international community continues to avoid directly targeting the foreign actors supplying and sustaining the warring factions. This gap between documented atrocity and enforcement action reflects the same geopolitical constraints that have paralyzed Sudan response efforts since the conflict began. The absence of pressure on external enablers makes a near-term reduction in violence unlikely regardless of UN findings.

sections.title: Military
sections.intro: U.S. military activity is dominated by active strikes against Iran, accelerating autonomous weapons development, and significant leadership and budget turbulence across multiple services.

items.headline: U.S. Conducts Second Wave of Strikes on Iranian Military Sites
items.summary: American forces struck Iranian military targets in a fresh round of attacks following the reimposition of a naval blockade on Iranian ports. This marks a significant escalation in direct U.S. military action against Iran, raising immediate questions about Iranian retaliation options and regional spillover. Watch for allied responses, Strait of Hormuz shipping disruptions, and any Iranian proxy activation.

items.headline: Air Force Validates Autonomous Combat Drone in First Live-Fire Test
items.summary: The YFQ-44A built by Anduril successfully completed the Air Force's first live-fire test for a Collaborative Combat Aircraft, a milestone in integrating autonomous wingmen alongside crewed fighters. The test validates a core pillar of next-generation air combat doctrine and accelerates procurement decisions. Concurrent Air Force moves toward mass-producible cheap cruise missiles signal a broader shift toward high-volume, lower-cost attritable systems.

items.headline: Ukraine Dismisses Defense Minister Fedorov After Six Months in a Cabinet Overhaul
items.summary: President Zelenskyy removed Mykhailo Fedorov from the defense ministry just six months after his appointment, signaling internal dissatisfaction with defense management amid ongoing war pressures. Rapid leadership turnover at the top of Ukraine's defense establishment introduces continuity risk at a critical procurement and battlefield planning juncture. The timing and scope of any broader cabinet restructuring will indicate whether this reflects strategic recalibration or political maneuvering.

items.headline: Space Force Faces Budget Cuts and Leadership Vacuum as Chief Prepares to Retire
items.summary: General Chance Saltzman's imminent retirement coincides with budget pressure on Space Force priorities and a congressional push to potentially dissolve the Space Development Agency back into the service. The leadership gap arrives at a moment when SDA is resuming delayed satellite launches critical to military communications and targeting infrastructure. How Congress resolves SDA's institutional future will have direct implications for U.S. space-based military capability timelines.

sections.title: Intel / OSINT
sections.intro: Intelligence oversight faces scrutiny on Capitol Hill while law enforcement actions highlight the intersection of surveillance technology, financial crime, and open-source data collection.

items.headline: DNI Nominee Clayton Faces Senate Pressure Over Election Integrity Positions
items.summary: Jay Clayton's confirmation hearing for Director of National Intelligence was dominated by questions about his past statements on voter fraud and the 2020 election, crowding out substantive discussion of intelligence priorities. The hearing signals that partisan tensions over election security will continue to shape oversight of the U.S. intelligence community. Watch whether Clayton's confirmation trajectory affects morale and operational continuity at ODNI during an already turbulent period for the IC.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: Dutch Police Dismantle Industrialized Crypto Fraud Network Spanning Multiple Countries
items.summary: Dutch authorities arrested the alleged ringleader of a crypto investment fraud operation that ran approximately 24 call centers, employed over 700 people posing as financial advisers, and operated continuously since at least 2021. The scale and corporate-like structure of the operation — resembling a legitimate multinational business — reflects a maturation of organized financial cybercrime that complicates detection and attribution. Investigators and financial regulators should note this as a model for future large-scale fraud enterprises.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

items.headline: LAPD Suspends Contract with License Plate Reader Firm Flock Safety Amid Growing Municipal Backlash
items.summary: The Los Angeles Police Department has paused its relationship with automated license plate recognition vendor Flock Safety, joining a growing list of U.S. agencies reconsidering mass surveillance partnerships. The move reflects increasing public and institutional scrutiny of ALPR data retention, sharing practices, and civil liberties implications. How Flock Safety responds — and whether other major cities follow — will shape the near-term trajectory of commercial surveillance infrastructure in U.S. law enforcement.
items.source: The Record from Recorded Future News

sections.title: ICS / SCADA / OT
sections.intro: Today's OT/ICS landscape is defined more by market and standards developments than active incidents, with post-quantum cryptography reaching a global milestone and vendor-side OT security investment accelerating.

items.headline: Classic McEliece Becomes First Post-Quantum Algorithm to Achieve ISO Standardization
items.summary: Post-Quantum's Classic McEliece algorithm has been formally incorporated into an ISO standard, marking the first post-quantum cryptography (PQC) algorithm to reach global standardization. For OT and industrial environments — where long-lived systems and communication protocols often operate for decades — this milestone is directly relevant, as adversaries may already be harvesting encrypted OT traffic for future decryption. Critical infrastructure operators should treat this as a concrete signal to begin PQC transition planning for legacy industrial protocols.

items.headline: Tosi Launches OT Network Intelligence Layer Targeting Industrial Traffic Analysis
items.summary: Tosi has expanded its Tosi Insight platform to U.S. customers, adding an intelligence layer designed to analyze OT network traffic and identify anomalies in industrial environments. The move reflects growing demand for passive visibility tools that can operate without disrupting sensitive industrial processes. Watch whether this gains traction in sectors like energy and water utilities, where network blind spots remain a persistent gap flagged by regulators.

items.headline: Corsha Expands Executive Team to Accelerate OT Security Product and Market Strategy
items.summary: Corsha, which focuses on machine identity and API security for OT environments, has appointed a new COO, CPO, and Chief Customer Officer — a leadership build-out signaling a push into broader OT market penetration. Machine-to-machine authentication remains a critical weakness in industrial control systems, where legacy devices often communicate with minimal credential verification. The executive investment suggests Corsha is positioning for competitive expansion as OT security spending increases across critical infrastructure sectors.
